'''Shmuel Onn''' ({{Langx|he|שמואל און}}; born 1960) is a [[mathematician]], [[Professor]] of [[Operations Research]] and Dresner Chair at the [[Technion - Israel Institute of Technology]].<ref>{{citation|title=Shmuel Onn|url=https://web.iem.technion.ac.il/site/academicstaff/shmuel-onn/|publisher=Technion}}</ref> He is known for his contributions to [[integer programming]] and nonlinear [[combinatorial optimization]].<ref name=book>{{citation|title=Shmuel Onn. Nonlinear discrete optimization: An algorithmic theory|url=https://bookstore.ams.org/emszlec-13|publisher=European Mathematical Society|date=2010}}</ref>

== Education ==
Shmuel Onn did his high school education in [[Kadoorie Agricultural High School]].<ref name=cv>{{citation|title=Abridged CV|url=https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Home-Page/abridged-cv.html|publisher=Technion|access-date=2021-09-30|archive-date=2021-11-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125154002/https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Home-Page/abridged-cv.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> He received his B.Sc. (Cum Laude) in [[Electrical Engineering]] from Technion in 1980, and following his obligatory service in the [[Israeli Navy|Navy]], received his M.Sc. from Technion in 1987.<ref name=cv/> Onn obtained his Ph.D. in operations research from [[Cornell University]], with minors in [[applied mathematics]] and [[computer science]], in 1992. His thesis, "Discrete Geometry, Group Representations and Combinatorial Optimization: an Interplay", was advised by [[Louis J. Billera]], [[Bernd Sturmfels]], and Leslie E. Trotter Jr.<ref>{{citation|title=Shmuel Onn|url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=91340|publisher=[[Mathematics Genealogy Project]]}}</ref>

During 1992–1993 he was a postdoctoral fellow at [[DIMACS]],<ref>{{citation|title=Past DIMACS Postdocs|url=http://dimacs.rutgers.edu/about/people/postdocs/past-dimacs-postdocs|publisher=[[Rutgers University]]}}</ref> and during 1993-1994 he was an [[Alexander von Humboldt Foundation|Alexander von Humboldt postdoctoral fellow]] at the [[University of Passau]], [[Germany]].<ref name=cv/>

== Career ==
In 1994 Onn joined the [[The William Davidson Faculty of Industrial Engineering & Management|Faculty of Data and Decision Sciences]] of Technion, where he is currently professor and Dresner Chair. He was also a Visiting Professor and Nachdiplom Lecturer at the [[Institute for Mathematical Research]], [[ETH]] [[Zürich]] in 2009,<ref name=eth>{{citation|title=Nachdiplom lectures - Past lectures|url=https://math.ethz.ch/fim/activities/nachdiplom-lectures/past-lectures.html|publisher=ETH}}</ref> and visiting professor at the Mathematics Department in the [[University of California, Davis]] (2001-2002).<ref>{{citation|title=Mathematics Colloquia and Seminars|url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/research/seminars?talk_id=663|publisher=University of California, Davis}}</ref> Professor Onn has been also a long-term visitor at various mathematical research institutes including [[Mittag-Leffler Institute|Mittag-Leffler]] in [[Stockholm]], [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute|MSRI]] in [[Berkeley, California|Berkeley]],<ref>{{citation|title=Personal Profile of Dr. Shmuel Onn|url=https://www.msri.org/people/2349|publisher=Mathematical Sciences Research Institute}}</ref> and [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]] in Germany.<ref>{{citation|title=Research in Pairs - 2007|url=https://www.mfo.de/scientific-program/long-term/research-in-pairs/rip-2007.pdf
|publisher=Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach}}</ref>
He also served as associate editor for ''[[Mathematics of Operations Research]]'' in 2010–2016<ref>{{citation|publisher=INFORMS|doi=10.1287/moor.2015.eb.v404|title=Editorial Board|journal=Mathematics of Operations Research|year=2015|volume=40|issue=4|pages=c2–c3|doi-access=free}}</ref> and associate editor for ''Discrete Optimization'' in 2004–2010.<ref name=cv/>

Onn advised several students and postdoctoral researchers who proceeded to pursue academic careers, including Antoine Deza, Sharon Aviran, Tal Raviv, Nir Halman, and Martin Koutecký.<ref>{{citation|title=Students and Postdoctorants|url=https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Home-Page/students-and-postdocs.html|publisher=Technion|access-date=2021-09-30|archive-date=2021-11-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125154004/https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Home-Page/students-and-postdocs.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Research ==
Shmuel Onn is known for his contributions to [[integer programming]] and nonlinear [[combinatorial optimization]]. In particular, he developed an algorithmic theory of linear and nonlinear integer programming in variable dimension using [[Graver bases]].<ref name=book/> This work introduced the theory of block-structured and n-fold integer programming,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Raymond Hemmecke|author2=Shmuel Onn|author3=Lyubov Romanchuk|title=N-fold integer programming in cubic time|journal=[[Mathematical Programming]]|year=2013|volume=137|pages=325–341|issue=1–2|doi=10.1007/s10107-011-0490-y|arxiv=1101.3267|s2cid=964450|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10107-011-0490-y}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=[[Jesús A. De Loera|Jesus De Loera]]|author2= Raymond Hemmecke|author3=Shmuel Onn|author4=Robert Weismantel|title= N-fold integer programming|journal=Discrete Optimization|series= In Memory of George B. Dantzig|year=2008|volume= 5|pages=231–241|issue=2|doi= 10.1016/j.disopt.2006.06.006|s2cid= 997926|doi-access=free}}</ref> and the broader theory of sparse and bounded tree-depth integer programming, shown to be fixed-parameter tractable.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Martin Koutecký|author2=Shmuel Onn|title=Sparse Integer Programming is FPT|journal=[[Bulletin of the European Association for Theoretical Computer Science]]|year=2021|volume=2|pages=69–71|issue=134|url=http://bulletin.eatcs.org/index.php/beatcs/article/view/660}}</ref><ref>{{cite arXiv|author1=[[Friedrich Eisenbrand]]|author2=Christoph Hunkenschroder|author3=Kim-Manuel Klein|author4=Martin Koutecký|author5=Asaf Levin|author6=Shmuel Onn|title=An algorithmic theory of integer programming|year=2019|class=math.OC|eprint=1904.01361}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Martin Koutecký|author2=Asaf Levin|author3=Shmuel Onn|title=A parameterized strongly polynomial algorithm for block structured integer programs|journal=[[ICALP]]|series=Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics (LIPIcs)|year=2018|volume=107|pages=85:1–85:14|doi=10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2018.85|doi-access=free |arxiv=1802.05859|isbn=9783959770767|s2cid=3336201|url=https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2018/9089/pdf/LIPIcs-ICALP-2018-85.pdf}}</ref>
These theories were followed up by other authors,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Jana Cslovjecsek|author2=Friedrich Eisenbrand|author3=Christoph Hunkenschroder|author4=Kim-Manuel Klein|author5=Lars Rohwedder|author6=Robert Weismantel|title=Block-Structured Integer and Linear Programming in Strongly Polynomial and Near Linear Time|journal=[[Symposium on Discrete Algorithms|SODA]]|year=2021|pages=1666–1681|arxiv=2002.07745|url=https://www.siam.org/conferences/cm/program/accepted-papers/soda21-accepted-papers}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Cornelius Brand|author2=Martin Koutecký|author3=Sebastian Ordyniak|title=Parameterized Algorithms for MILPs with Small Treedepth|journal=[[AAAI]]|year=2021|volume=35|issue=14|pages=12249–12257|doi=10.1609/aaai.v35i14.17454 |arxiv=1912.03501|s2cid=208909901 |url=https://ojs.aaai.org/index.php/AAAI/article/view/17454}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Timothy F. N. Chan|author2=Jacob W. Cooper|author3=Martin Koutecký|author4=Daniel Král'|author5=Kristýna Pekárková|title=Matrices of Optimal Tree-Depth and Row-Invariant Parameterized Algorithm for Integer Programming|journal=[[ICALP ]]|year=2020|pages=26:1–26:19|arxiv=1907.06688|url=https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2020/12433/pdf/LIPIcs-ICALP-2020-26.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Klaus Jansen|author2=Alexandra Lassota|author3=Lars Rohwedder|title=Near-Linear Time Algorithm for n-fold ILPs via Color Coding|journal=ICALP|series=Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics (LIPIcs)|year=2019|volume=132|pages=75:1–75:13|doi=10.4230/LIPIcs.ICALP.2019.75|doi-access=free |isbn=9783959771092|s2cid=53300379|url=https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2019/10651/}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|author1=Eduard Eiben|author2=Robert Ganian|author3=Dusan Knop|author4=Kim-Manuel Klein|author5=Sebastian Ordyniak|author6=Michal Pilipczuk|author7=Marcin Wrochna|title=Integer Programming and Combinatorial Optimization|chapter=Integer Programming and Incidence Treedepth |series=Lecture Notes in Computer Science|year=2019|volume=11480|pages=194–204|arxiv=2012.00079|url=http://www.cs.ox.ac.uk/Stanislav.Zivny/publications/Eiben19ipco-preprint.pdf|doi=10.1007/978-3-030-17953-3_15 |isbn=978-3-030-17953-3|s2cid=142503705}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Friedrich Eisenbrand|author2=Christoph Hunkenschröder|author3=Kim-Manuel Klein|title=Faster Algorithms for Integer Programs with Block Structure|journal=ICALP|year=2018|pages=49:1–49:13|arxiv=1802.06289|url=https://drops.dagstuhl.de/opus/volltexte/2018/9053/pdf/LIPIcs-ICALP-2018-49.pdf}}</ref> and have applications in a variety of areas.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Dusan Knop|author2=Martin Koutecký|author3=Matthias Mnich|title=Voting and Bribing in Single-Exponential Time|journal=ACM Transactions on Economics and Computation|year=2020|volume=8|issue=3|pages=12:1–12:28|doi=10.1145/3396855|s2cid=218529858|doi-access=free|arxiv=1812.01852}}</ref>
<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Robert Bredereck|author2=Piotr Faliszewski|author3=Rolf Niedermeier|author4=Piotr Skowron|author5=Nimrod Talmon|author3-link=Rolf Niedermeier|title=Mixed integer programming with convex/concave constraints: Fixed-parameter tractability and applications to multicovering and voting|journal=[[Theoretical Computer Science (journal)|Theoretical Computer Science]]|year=2020|volume=814|pages=86–105|doi=10.1016/j.tcs.2020.01.017|arxiv=1709.02850|s2cid=3227033|url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S030439752030044X}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Dusan Knop|author2=Martin Koutecký|author3=Matthias Mnich|title=Combinatorial n-fold integer programming and applications|journal=[[Mathematical Programming]]|year=2020|volume=184|issue=1|pages=1–34|doi=10.1007/s10107-019-01402-2|s2cid=213316783|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10107-019-01402-2|arxiv=1705.08657 |hdl=11420/4607 }}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Klaus Jansen|author2=Kim-Manuel Klein|author3=Marten Maack|author4=Malin Rau|title=Empowering the Configuration-IP - New PTAS Results for Scheduling with Setups Times|journal=ITCS - Innovations in Theoretical Computer Science|series=Leibniz International Proceedings in Informatics (LIPIcs)|year=2019|volume=124|pages=44:1–44:19|doi=10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2019.44|doi-access=free |isbn=9783959770958|s2cid=24006600}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Dusan Knop|author2=Martin Koutecký|title=Scheduling meets n-fold integer programming|journal=Journal of Scheduling|year=2018|volume=21|issue=5|pages=493–503|doi=10.1007/s10951-017-0550-0|arxiv=1603.02611|s2cid=9627563|url=https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10951-017-0550-0}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Lin Chen|author2=Dániel Marx|title=Covering a tree with rooted subtrees - parameterized and approximation algorithms|journal=SODA|year=2018|pages=2801–2820|url=https://www.cs.bme.hu/~dmarx/papers/lin-marx-soda2018.pdf}}</ref>

Some other contributions of Onn include a framework that uses edge-directions for solving
convex multi-criteria combinatorial optimization problems and its applications,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Shmuel Onn|author2=[[Uriel Rothblum]]|title=Convex combinatorial optimization|journal=[[Discrete & Computational Geometry]]|year=2004|volume=32|issue=4|pages=549–566|doi=10.1007/s00454-004-1138-y|s2cid=803661|url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s00454-004-1138-y.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Eric Babson|author2=Shmuel Onn|author3=[[Rekha Thomas]]|title=The Hilbert zonotope and a polynomial time algorithm for universal Grobner bases|journal=[[Advances in Applied Mathematics]]|year=2003|volume=30|issue=3|pages=529–544|doi=10.1016/S0196-8858(02)00509-2|s2cid=7178467|doi-access=free|arxiv=math/0207135}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Frank Hwang|author2=Shmuel Onn|author3=Uriel Rothblum|title=A polynomial time algorithm for shaped partition problems|journal=[[SIAM Journal on Optimization]]|year=1999|volume=10|pages=70–81|doi=10.1137/S1052623497344002|url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/S1052623497344002|url-access=subscription}}</ref> a universality theorem showing that every integer program is one over slim three-dimensional tables,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Jesus De Loera|author2=Shmuel Onn|title=All linear and integer programs are slim 3-way transportation programs|journal=SIAM Journal on Optimization|year=2006|volume=17|issue=3|pages=806–821|doi=10.1137/040610623|url=https://www.math.ucdavis.edu/~deloera/researchsummary/universalitytransportation.pdf}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|author1=Jesus De Loera|author2=Shmuel Onn|title=The complexity of three-way statistical tables|journal=[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]|year=2004|volume=33|issue=4|pages=819–836|doi=10.1137/S0097539702403803|arxiv=math/0207200|s2cid=14941545|url=https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Selected/SIAMJC1.pdf}}</ref> the settling of the complexity of hypergraph degree sequences,<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Antoine Deza|author2=Asaf Levin|author3=Syed M. Meesum|author4=Shmuel Onn|title=Optimization over degree sequences|journal=[[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]|year=2018|volume=32|issue=3|pages=2067–2079|doi=10.1137/17M1134482|arxiv=1706.03951|s2cid=52039639|url=https://epubs.siam.org/doi/abs/10.1137/17M1134482}}</ref>
and the introduction of colorful linear programming.<ref>{{cite journal|author1=[[Imre Bárány]]|author2=Shmuel Onn|title=Colourful linear programming and its relatives|journal=Mathematics of Operations Research|year=1997|volume=22|issue=3|pages=550–567|doi=10.1287/moor.22.3.550|url=https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Selected/MOR97.pdf|access-date=2021-09-23|archive-date=2021-11-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211125154005/https://ie.technion.ac.il/~onn/Selected/MOR97.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Honors and awards ==
* 2010, [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences|INFORMS]] Computing Society (ICS) Prize.<ref>{{citation|title=Shmuel Onn - 2010 INFORMS Computing Society Prize|url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Award-Recipients/Shmuel-Onn|publisher=INFORMS}}</ref>
* 2009, [https://math.ethz.ch/fim/activities/nachdiplom-lectures.html Nachdiplom Lecturer], Institute for Mathematical Research, ETH Zürich.<ref name=eth/> 
 
== Books ==
* Nonlinear discrete optimization: An algorithmic theory. Zurich Lectures in Advanced Mathematics. [[European Mathematical Society]] (EMS), Zürich, 2010.<ref name=book/>

== Personal life ==
Shmuel is married to Ruth. They have two children, Amos and Naomi, and live in [[Haifa]].
